newsitem.title: UK: Cricket-Elliot leads Australian run charge.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Elliot leads Australian run charge.

text.p: Matthew Elliott drove and pulled his way to a spectacular century on Sunday as Australia refused to concede rain had cost them the opportunity to square the Ashes series against England

In a frenzied 17.4 overs when play finally began on the fourth day of the disrupted second test at Lord's, Elliott advanced from 55 to 112 while Australia took their overnight 131 for two to 213 for seven, a lead of 136 with one day remaining.

A succession of torrential downpours prevented any play until 5.40 p.m. (1640GMT) and a washout looked probable. But the rain held off for once, the covers were taken off and the Australians leaped with delight on the team balcony when they learned they had another chance to get after England.
In a raucous atmosphere resembling a one-day final more than a test match, Elliott needed only 45 balls to reach his hundred.
When he was finally out, caught mishooking Andrew Caddick, he had batted for 242 minutes and scored 20 fours from 180 deliveries. Eleven of his boundaries came in Sunday's brief session.
The tall Victorian left-hander was fully conscious of the significance of a century at world cricket's headquarters.
"It's a pretty special place," he said. "It's everything, it's the Long Room, the Pavilion and the ground and all the people who come here, it's the whole package."
Elliott, who benefited from a bad miss by Devon Malcolm on Saturday when he skied a hook shot, took some blows on the body from Darren Gough and later needed ice on his elbow.
But he played a series of classic cover-drives with the right elbow high and some blistering pull shots.
He also continued to push the score along while Mark Waugh (33), Shane Warne (nought), Steve Waugh (nought) and Michael Bevan (four) perished at the other end.

Mark Waugh sliced Caddick to Malcolm at third man, Warne, promoted to push the scoring along, lasted only four balls before slashing Gough high to Nasser Hussain in the gully, Steve Waugh was lbw to Caddick while Bevan was caught behind off the England paceman.
Further rain is forecast for Monday and the weather is still likely to have the final say.
Thursday's opening day was abandoned without a ball being bowled and only 92 minutes' play were possible on Friday.
But Elliott and Glenn McGrath, who took eight for 38 from 20.3 overs of controlled fire in England's first innings of 77, have given the Australian an outside chance of victory.

McGrath will have to produce something similar on Monday if Australia are to square the six-test series but Elliott reflected the determination in the Australian camp when he said they would be pressing for victory from the opening ball.
